Information since September points to a still-strong labor market and moderate growth, but weak business fixed investment and soft exports with inflation below 2% imply downside risks. In line with investment-driven business-cycle dynamics—where declines in investment can materially drag real GDP—the rate cut and “ample reserves” operations seek to bolster demand and ease money-market frictions. Given the centrality of expectations in inflation dynamics (e.g., New Keynesian Phillips curve estimates by Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido; Rudebusch) and evidence that monetary policy has short-run real effects (Sims’ VARs; McCallum & Nelson; B. Friedman), this stance is supportive but cautiously so, as persistently low inflation compensation and soft capex temper the outlook.
